body:
#2019 TOOK THE INJECTION REMEDY AND YOUR ADDED CONSTRAINT IS SATISFIED. New
head dd1285fb63, still CHANGES REQUESTED for other reasons, but the deadline
question is closed.

    PRODUCT_NOTICE_DEADLINE   from_secs(1)   UNCHANGED
    AIDA_TEST_NOTICE_DEADLINE_MS             per-subprocess override

The product's bound did not move. That was the thing you said the injection
would otherwise swallow — a test value becoming the product's answer with
nobody choosing — and it did not happen. BUG-1239's fail-open bound for an
advisory per-turn notice is intact.

I CHECKED THE SCOPING RATHER THAN THE DESIGN, because an injectable deadline
set in a helper would have recreated the conflict silently:

    one cmd.env, inside awaiting_notice_tracks_real_lease_through_session_end
    fn at :212, injection at :278 — not a helper, not global

So awaiting_notice_does_not_read_an_open_stdin_pipe still runs against the 1s
default, which is the short bound it needs. AND THE COMMENT AT THE INJECTION
SITE NAMES THAT SIBLING TEST EXPLICITLY as the reason the bound must stay
short for every other caller. A fix that writes down the constraint it must
not break, at the one place where breaking it would be tempting.

NEW FINDING, SMALL BUT IT HAS A NAMED HOME: AIDA_TEST_NOTICE_DEADLINE_MS IS
UNDOCUMENTED. CLAUDE.md gives every AIDA_* variable one canonical reference,
docs/environment-variables.md, and requires the row IN THE SAME CHANGE. Zero
occurrences there; the commit touches two files and neither is that one. Same
class as the SPEC-IDs-in-user-facing-text rule — cheap to satisfy, invisible
until someone greps the canonical doc for a variable that exists, and the
omission is what makes a canonical reference stop being canonical.

STILL BLOCKING AND UNTOUCHED by this two-file commit: the no-recompiles half
of the warm-verify criterion, the unanswered punt from 2026-09-19, and the
trailer strip.

PIPELINE 319 IS RUNNING ON THIS HEAD and I will read its test job when it
terminates — including if the stdin test fails again, which would mean the
injection did not scope as I have just read it. 318's red belongs to
442a63243c and is not evidence about this sha; I have recorded that on the
verdict so nobody reads the older result against the newer commit.

ONE THING WORTH NAMING ABOUT THE SEQUENCE: this branch has now produced three
heads in an hour — dropped the fix, restored it, then replaced it with a
better one. The middle step looked like a regression and the last two look
like churn, but the actual trajectory is a root cause found, a wrong remedy
measured, and the right remedy derived FROM the measurement. Pipeline 318's
red is what made 319 possible. A board that counted heads would read this
branch as thrashing; a board that reads the reds sees it converging.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2019 took the injection - product bound stays 1s, your constraint holds. Wiring scoped to ONE cmd.env and the comment names the sibling test. New finding: the env var is undocumented
